name: VIJAY AMRITRAJ
coach: N/A (Retired; formerly trained by family and Indian coaches)
bio:
Career Overview: Playing Style: A graceful all-court player with a strong serve-and-volley game and excellent touch, adept on grass and hard courts.
Career-High ATP Singles Ranking: #16 (July 7, 1980), Career-High ATP Doubles Ranking: #23 (March 24, 1980).
Best Grand Slam Singles Performance: Reached the quarterfinals of Wimbledon (1973, 1981) and the US Open (1973, 1974).
Notable Achievements: ATP Titles: Won 16 singles and 13 doubles titles during the 1970s and 1980s. Davis Cup & National Representation: Led India to the Davis Cup finals in 1974 and 1987, one of India’s greatest Davis Cup heroes with a record of 45-18 in singles and doubles combined.
Other Highlights: A trailblazer for Indian tennis in the Open Era, defeating top players like Rod Laver and John McEnroe. Later became a successful commentator, actor (e.g., James Bond film *Octopussy*), and philanthropist.
Amritraj retired in 1993, leaving a lasting legacy as one of India’s finest tennis players. 🎾🇮🇳
